findings.desc: review-convergence.ts:253 assessReviewConvergence has an undocumented precondition that perRoundBlockingCounts.length >= STALL_WINDOW (3) for the strictlyDecreasing branch to work correctly. When called directly with a shorter array (e.g. assessReviewConvergence(4,[2,1])), strictlyDecreasing = (window.length === STALL_WINDOW) evaluates to false regardless of values, causing a FALSE POSITIVE stall for genuinely decreasing sequences like [2,1]. The production caller assessReviewConvergenceAtEntry is safe because STALL_MIN_ROUNDS-1 (3) >= STALL_WINDOW (3) guarantees a full window, but this invariant is undocumented and unenforced — future direct callers can silently trigger false positives. Fix: add a JSDoc precondition note to assessReviewConvergence stating that perRoundBlockingCounts must be dense with length >= STALL_WINDOW when roundCount >= STALL_MIN_ROUNDS, or assert window.length >= STALL_WINDOW before the strictlyDecreasing check and return stalled=false (conservative) for short windows.
